title: Low-Degree Representations of Alternating-Moduli Outputs
summary: For alternating-moduli outputs, the low-degree obstruction is proved only over fields of order a power of three; exact representation or accurate approximation over arbitrary fixed polynomial rings remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the outputs of the $(2,3)$ one-way-function and pseudorandom-function constructions, whose coordinates are sums modulo $3$ of values that are themselves sums modulo $2$ of secret-input bits, can be represented exactly or approximated sufficiently accurately by low-degree polynomials over any fixed polynomial ring. Existing rigorous analysis covers the shared modulus-switching map $\{0,1\}^{\ell}\to\mathbb{Z}_3$, given by $x\mapsto\sum_i x_i\bmod 3$, only for polynomials over $\mathrm{GF}(3^r)$, for every $r\ge 1$. Prove the analogous impossibility for arbitrary polynomial rings or refute it by constructing such a representation or approximation, and determine the resulting applicability of linearization-based algebraic attacks.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of the (2,3) alternating-moduli one-way-function and pseudorandom-function constructions.
parameters: ℓ: number of input bits for the shared modulus-switching map
r ≥ 1: extension degree in the known field family GF(3^r)
fixed polynomial ring: ambient setting for the sought low-degree representation or approximation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove the analogous impossibility over arbitrary polynomial rings or construct an exact representation or sufficiently accurate low-degree approximation, and determine whether linearization-based algebraic attacks apply.

citations.label: MPC-Friendly Symmetric Cryptography from Alternating Moduli: Candidates, Protocols, and Applications

progress.summary: The source explicitly conjectures that the outputs cannot be represented or well approximated by low-degree polynomials over any fixed polynomial ring. It reports rigorous coverage only over GF(3^r) for every r at least one and links the unresolved extension to linearization attacks.
